sections.h2: How do you reach Bladen County Tax Administration?
sections.html:
Tax Administration sits at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, and walk-in hours run weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. Letters go to PO Box 385, Elizabethtown, NC 28337. Phone 910-862-6730 or write to bctax@bladenco.org.

An online portal shows bills and takes payments, and an automated line at 1-877-369-0025 takes payments by phone. The county's property record search is a separate tool, and the FAQ points owners to bladen.ustaxdata.com for prior-year assessments.

The 2026 tax year brought a change: the county now collects for four towns, East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake and Elizabethtown. Owners inside those towns should ask Tax Administration how the town portion appears on the bill.

sections.h2: What is Bladen County like, and what does that mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The county describes itself as a Coastal Plain county in southeastern North Carolina, about 879 square miles, which makes it the fourth largest in the state. The Cape Fear River bisects it, White Lake is commercially developed for visitors, and Jones and Singletary Lakes are state parks.

QuickFacts lists 30,007 people for July 2025. That is 1.3% above the 2020 base, yet far below the 35,190 of 2010. Home values are modest: the 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $135,100, versus $332,700 for the nation. Owners hold 69.2% of the housing stock by the Census rate, median gross rent is $773, and the county issued 97 building permits in 2025.

The county names food processing, manufacturing and assembly, textiles, chemicals and agribusiness as its industry base, with workforce training at Bladen Community College. Against a $135,100 median, even a small back-tax or title problem looms large.

sections.h2: Did Bladen County's 2026 revaluation change my 2026 tax bill?
sections.html:
No. The General Assembly postponed Bladen's new values by a year, so 2026 bills use the older 2025 values and the 2026 reappraisal values first apply for the 2027 tax year.

The county completed a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026, with a contracted appraisal firm, and mailed notices to all real property owners on March 9, 2026. The reappraisal before that dated from 2022. Then S.L. 2026-8 and S.L. 2026-47 imposed a one-year moratorium. The legislative staff summary lists Bladen among nine counties subject to it: Anson, Bladen, Buncombe, Chowan, Davidson, Guilford, Onslow, Pamlico and Pender.

A School of Government analysis of the first bill notes that counties must still list and appraise changes found during the reappraisal, such as an unrecorded building, but use the older schedule of values. It also says counties should send notice of the new values again in 2027. The 2027 value is the one that will drive your bill, so confirm where your parcel stands with Tax Administration at 910-862-6730 before you list.

sections.h2: How do appeals work after the Bladen reappraisal?
sections.html:
The county asked for appeals on its 2026 notices by April 10, 2026, a date now past. The two session laws separately give taxpayers in the affected counties the right to appeal 2026 values during calendar year 2026, and the School of Government reads that as running through December 31, 2026.

Bladen's FAQ rules out affordability as a basis. What counts is an assessment out of line with similar properties, or a factual mistake on the record card. Get the card first, then collect a private appraisal, comparable sales, a survey or photos of structural damage.

  • By mail to the revaluation team, PO Box 774, Elizabethtown, NC 28337
  • In the marked box in the lobby of the tax office on E King Street
  • In the drop box in the lot behind the county courthouse

Formal appeals go to the board of equalization and review, which opens in the window from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May and, in a reappraisal year, wraps up by December 1. After the board mails its ruling, the owner has 30 days to take it to the Property Tax Commission.

sections.h2: How does Bladen County's tax rate compare with other 2026 reappraisal counties?
sections.html:
NCDOR's 2024-25 schedule prints Bladen at $.7850 per $100, and the county commissioners' association map book shows 0.7850 again for fiscal year 2026-27. Bladen is one of several counties that were scheduled to reappraise in 2026.

Bladen's FAQ treats appraisal and tax rate as separate decisions: values come first, and the commissioners fix the rate in June from the budget. A higher value alone does not raise a bill.

sections.h2: When is Bladen County tax due and what relief can owners apply for?
sections.html:
Bladen bills use the state calendar. September 1 is the due date, January 5 is the last interest-free day, 2% attaches January 6, and three-fourths of a percent more accrues monthly from February 1. The statutory listing period for property runs through January 31.

Tax Administration posts two application deadlines:

  • June 1 is the cutoff for new elderly, disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker applications.
  • January 31 is the cutoff for new applications on everything else, including religious, charitable and present-use valuation.

For 2026, NCDOR prints a $38,800 income limit for the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, plus $58,200 as the higher circuit breaker ceiling. The disabled veteran exclusion takes $45,000 off appraised value with no age or income test. Only one of the three programs can apply to an owner, and the circuit breaker is renewed by a fresh application each year.

sections.h2: What does a seller need to know about taxes and deeds in Bladen County?
sections.html:
Before a deed is recorded in Bladen, taxes have to be accounted for. Either the filer completes a certification form, or a closing attorney prepares the deed and it states that delinquent taxes, if any, will be paid by the attorney to the county tax collector when closing proceeds are disbursed.

This route lets a house with back taxes close: the attorney pays the delinquent bills out of the sale money, and the deed then goes to the register. The seller also pays the $1.00 per $500 excise tax before recording.

A parcel that fails to sell at a county tax foreclosure auction becomes county property and stays on the market. Bladen keeps a public list of those parcels, updated November 2, 2026. State law gives the auction a deposit of up to 20% and a 10-day window for higher bids after the report of sale. Before confirmation, paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs redeems the property.

faqs.q: How do I call Bladen County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: Dial 910-862-6730. Visits are at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Why does my 2026 Bladen bill not reflect the new reappraisal?
faqs.a: The General Assembly postponed the reappraisal by a year for Bladen and eight other counties. Bills for 2026 use the 2025 values, and the new values start with the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Has the Bladen County appeal window closed?
faqs.a: The county's April 10, 2026 date is past, but the session laws allow appeals of 2026 values through calendar year 2026. A fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round, so call the office to confirm your status.

faqs.q: When do Bladen homeowners apply for elderly, disabled or veteran tax relief?
faqs.a: New applications for those programs and the circuit breaker are due June 1 yearly. Other exemptions and deferments, such as present-use value, are due January 31.

faqs.q: Can a Bladen County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing attorney pays the delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from your proceeds, and the deed says so. The sale has to close before the court confirms any tax foreclosure sale.
